admission.justification: Compatibility contrast and deferral were both weighed with their grounds for return, and the chosen refusal binds every future start, lifecycle route and vocabulary change.

alternatives.option: Refuse the disabled mode at the start on every repository and remove it now, keeping old contracts readable with abandon as the way out.
alternatives.reason: The mode works end to end nowhere, so no working case is preserved by keeping it, and readability plus abandon keeps every existing contract recoverable.

alternatives.option: Keep a compatibility contrast that lets a disabled task close out and integrate without memory, as the withdrawn packet proposed.
alternatives.reason: It lands code with no invariant judgment on converted ground, which the direction forbids.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A future mode gains a working end-to-end lifecycle with its own gate, so opting out stops meaning escaping judgment.

alternatives.option: Defer the removal to a later leaf and refuse only where knowledge exists.
alternatives.reason: The mode is unusable on unconverted ground too, and a partial refusal preserves the strand-everywhere failure it was meant to fix.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A repository is found where a disabled task completes its whole lifecycle today.

consequences: Every start, lifecycle route, CLI surface, skill text and test fixture treats disabled as removed; old contracts are read and abandoned, never converted in place.
context: MIK-R49 proved a task could opt out of memory and land code with no gate on converted ground, contradicting the mandatory-invariant-work direction; the landed code instead stranded every disabled task, which could be started but never closed, synced, integrated, cleaned up or abandoned.
decider: Developer direction D5 and D47 with the architect's run-2 rulings of 2026-10-04.
